panel.summary: Forked `lheading` will silently drift from upstream on markdown-it upgrades
panel.evidence: `lheadingRule` (lines 70-155) is a full copy of markdown-it 14.x's rule installed via `md.block.ruler.at('lheading', ...)`, so any upstream bug fix or CommonMark spec correction to `lheading` in a `^14` patch/minor bump is silently discarded — the copy keeps whatever markdown-it 14.1 did, with nothing in CI comparing the two. A wrapper that delegates to the original fn and only vetoes the lone-dash case (as is done for `list`) would not have this drift.

coderabbit.summary: Missing over-indent guard in `isEmptyBulletLine` (defensive parity with `lheadingRule`).
coderabbit.detail: **Missing over-indent guard in `isEmptyBulletLine` (defensive parity with `lheadingRule`).** `lheadingRule` explicitly bails when `state.sCount[startLine] - state.blkIndent >= 4` (Line 74) before treating a line as a candidate underline, mirroring markdown-it's own "over-indented lines are lazy continuation" rule. `isEmptyBulletLine` has no equivalent check, so in principle a heavily-indented (`>=4` spaces beyond `blkIndent`) empty-bullet-shaped line could be treated as a paragraph terminator by `wrappedList` even though it should stay part of the paragraph's lazy continuation. In practice this is likely harmless: markdown-it's `paragraph` block rule almost certainly `continue`s past such over-indented lines (the same pattern is visible in the forked `lheadingRule` loop) before ever calling terminator rules, so `wrappedList` probably never sees this case in silent mode. Worth a quick confirmation/test with a heavily-indented dash line to be sure, or add the guard defensively for self-consistency with the rest of the file.
